repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend at 406e300 (main, EUDPA-675): the Import Notification Service front door, a Hapi + Nunjucks + govuk-frontend Node app. All paths below are from the repo root. Its user-facing pages live in src/server/app/features/: dashboard/ (the notifications dashboard at /, ~525 lines with its fit spec; reads the ins-backend read model through src/server/app/services/ins-backend/) and address-book/ (list /address-book, add /address-book/add, view /address-book/{id}, edit /address-book/{id}/edit, delete /address-book/{id}/delete, ~2,600 lines with copy, view models, the handshake to a journey (handshake-context.js, journey-registry.js) and 5 fit specs; backed by src/server/app/services/address-book/ and services/countries/). features/index.js registers those six controllers; src/server/app/routes.js adds features/address-lookup-spike/ (a postcode lookup spike, ~550 lines) only in dev or local environments. Shared pieces: src/server/app/shared/ (layout.njk, copy.en.js/copy.cy.js, kit.js, paths.js, error.njk, error-summary.njk, ~390 lines), src/server/app/auth/unauthorised.njk, src/server/auth/ (sign-in, sign-out, organisation routes, stub sign-in, ~300 lines), src/plugins/auth.js and csrf.js, src/server/app/lib/validate/ (validators, ~420 lines), src/server/common/constants/journey-set-bases.js (where the animals and plants journeys live), the repo-level fit/ smoke spec and sign-in helper, and the feature docs in src/server/app/docs/ (~940 lines). Every page's copy has English and Welsh files. In scope: the dashboard and address book features, shared layout and copy, the journey handshake to the animals frontend, and the fit specs. Left out: the vitest unit tests (*.test.js; behaviour is read from the source they test), src/config/ and src/server/common/helpers/ infrastructure (logging, redis, metrics, CSP, static files), src/client/stylesheets, health check, build and lint config, lighthouse config and generated reports, coverage/, test-results/ and playwright-report/. No rulings ledger (no decisions.json or equivalent) exists in the repo; the docs folder is the nearest record of intent. Cut into 5 parts by what a user sees: dashboard; address book list, view and delete; address book add, edit and handshake; shared layout, sign-in and docs; the dev-only address lookup spike.

Extracted in 5 parts:
Part 1, Notifications dashboard: Part 1, Notifications dashboard, read in full at repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend 406e300 (main): features/dashboard/controller.js (129 lines: GET / handler, page/sort/referenceNumber query parsing, table row and View link building, error path), template.njk (89 lines: h1, search form, sort form, empty state, no-results state, results label, clear-search link, govukTable, govukPagination), view-model/list.js (119 lines: sort options, date format, query string, results label, pagination, notification links into the live-animals journey), copy/copy.en.js and copy/copy.cy.js (34 and 35 lines, identical key trees), dashboard.fit.spec.js (119 lines: AC1/AC2, axe, AC3 submitted, AC3 draft, AC4, AC5), services/ins-backend/client.js, index.js and stub.js (GET /notifications client, stub-mode switch, four-notification stub), common/constants/journey-set-bases.js (only /live-animals) and shared/paths.js (dashboardPath and inDashboardSection only claimed here). Also looked at common/helpers/set-base-url.js and common/services/mode.js to resolve the journey link base and stub-mode rule. Covered: the one page at /, its heading (no caption), search field and button, sort select and button, empty state with 'Start a new notification', 'No notifications found' with Clear search, results label, the six-column table with its raw status text (no tags), View links to notification-view or the journey hub, pagination, the 500 recoverable-error path, the ins-backend request and response shape, the stub dataset and rules, every fit test, and the Welsh copy. Found no filter beyond reference search, no plants link, no status tags and no organisation scoping in the frontend request; each is recorded as a claim or gap.
Part 2, Address book list, view and delete: Part 2, Address book list, view and delete. Read in full: the list feature (list/list.controller.js, list/list.njk, view-model/list.js), the view feature (view/view.controller.js, view/view.njk), the delete feature (delete/delete.controller.js, delete/delete.njk), the shared helpers stored-address.js, address-id-params.js and success-banner.js, the client script src/client/javascripts/address-book-success-banner.js, the English and Welsh copy (copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js; only the list, successBanner, view and delete keys are claimed here, plus the form.fields labels the view page reuses), the address book service (services/address-book/client.js, index.js, stub.js) and the fit specs list.fit.spec.js (6 tests), view.fit.spec.js (5 tests), delete.fit.spec.js (4 tests) with their helpers axe.js and seed-address.js. Shared paths.js and kit.js (base, requireOrganisationId, pageRoutes) and the shared recoverableError copy were read only where these pages call them. Pages covered: GET /address-book (search form, add button, empty state, no-match state, results label, table, pagination, success banner, recoverable error), GET /address-book/{id} (summary list, Edit and Delete buttons, Back link, not-found path), GET and POST /address-book/{id}/delete (confirmation, confirm, cancel, banner, redirect). Service: list, get and delete calls, organisation scoping and the in-memory stub. Every test in the three specs has a claim. The add and edit pages, the handshake and the country list loader belong to other parts.
Part 3, Address book add, edit and journey handshake: Part 3, address book add, edit and journey handshake, read in full from repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend: features/address-book/add/ (add.controller.js 152 lines, add.njk 118), edit/ (edit.controller.js 138, edit.njk 111), fields.js (field rules and the Joi rule set), address-countries.js (country list for the select, GB pinned first), handshake-context.js and journey-registry.js (the journey handshake with the animals frontend), copy/copy.en.js and copy.cy.js (add, edit, form, errors and success-banner keys claimed; list, view and delete keys left to part 2), lib/validate/ (index.js, run.js, validators.js, calendar.js: the shared Joi validators), services/countries/ (client.js, index.js, stub.js: reference-data countries with a process-wide cache and a four-country stub) and services/address-book/client.js (create and update calls with organisation scoping), plus the fit specs add.fit.spec.js (19 tests once the required and max-length loops expand) and edit.fit.spec.js (7 tests) with their helpers address-form.js and axe.js. To ground what the read files call, I also looked at shared/kit.js (error summary, page title, organisation check), shared/paths.js, services/address-book/index.js (API error mapping), features/address-book/address-id-params.js, stored-address.js, success-banner.js, common/constants/journey-set-bases.js and common/helpers/set-base-url.js. Covered: the add page at /address-book/add (heading, two section headings, nine fields with labels, hint, autocomplete, widths and required/optional, country options and their source, save and cancel, Cache-Control), the edit page at /address-book/{id}/edit (id check, prefill, back link, save, cancel, not-found and deleted handling), every validation rule and its English and Welsh message, how the error summary links to fields and values are preserved, server-side validation and failure states, the create and update payloads and organisation scoping, the success banners, the handshake (one registered journey type gbn-ag to the animals frontend's live-animals set, four query parameters, all-or-none rule, session storage, hidden fields, the cancel label, the return URL with handshake-token and addressId), the shared validators and calendar helpers the address form does and does not use, and every test in both fit specs. Gaps recorded where the slice is silent: no caption, no handshake on edit, no fit test of the handshake, no postcode or phone format rule, no verification of the handshake token.
Part 4, Shared layout, sign-in and feature docs: Part 4 of repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend at 406e300: the chrome around every page, sign-in, and the repo's own docs. Read in full: README.md; the seven docs under src/server/app/docs/ (README, features, architecture, services, add-a-page, testing; lighthouse.md is linked but not in this part's read list); src/server/app/shared/ (layout.njk, copy.js, copy.en.js, copy.cy.js, copy-leaves.js, kit.js, paths.js, error.njk, error-summary.njk); src/server/app/auth/unauthorised.njk; src/server/app/features/index.js and routes.js; src/server/router.js; src/server/auth/ (index.js, controller.js, stub-sign-in.js); src/plugins/auth.js and csrf.js; src/config/nunjucks/context/context.js; src/client/javascripts/application.js; fit/smoke.fit.spec.js and fit/sign-in.js; and the workspace page docs/repos/trade-imports-ins-frontend.md. To say what the error page and the sign-in redirects show, three small helpers the read files call were also read: src/server/common/helpers/errors.js (catchAll), src/auth/get-safe-redirect.js and src/auth/get-sign-out-url.js. Covered: the layout (title pattern, GOV.UK header, service navigation and which item is current, phase banner, back link, recoverable-error banner, journey strip, footer, skip link, no language toggle); every shared copy key in English and Welsh, plus the validator default messages; the error summary, the error page per status and the unauthorised page; the Defra ID routes (/auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-in-oidc, /auth/sign-out, /auth/sign-out-oidc, /auth/organisation), the session strategy and its redirect to sign-in, the stub-mode sign-in and sign-out routes (there is no stub sign-in form: it signs in on a GET); CSRF; the full route table and the dev/local-only spike; the single smoke test; and every rule the docs record about the dashboard, address book, handshake, copy, services, tests and boundaries. The workspace page disagrees with the repo in places (INS_MODE/AUTH_STUB_MODE vs STUB_MODE, Vite vs webpack, README described as template text); each is recorded as its own claim with a note, not reconciled.
Part 5, Address lookup spike (dev only): Part 5, Address lookup spike (dev only). Read in full: the spike feature folder src/server/app/features/address-lookup-spike/ (controller.js, template.njk, detect-search-mode.js, map-to-address-fields.js, is-dev-or-local.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js) and the address lookup service src/server/app/services/address-lookup/ (client.js, index.js, stub.js). For context only, read the lines that register the spike in src/server/app/routes.js, the pageRoutes/base/SURFACES helpers in src/server/app/shared/kit.js, src/server/common/services/mode.js (stub mode), the spike section of src/server/app/docs/features.md and the registration tests in src/server/router.test.js. The slice is one temporary page, /address-lookup-spike (EUDPA-390), registered only when the CDP environment is dev or local. It has one search box that decides between a postcode search and a free-text search, a results list with a 'Use this address' button per result, a 'Where the time went' timings table, three warning states, and a mapped view that shows how a chosen result would fill the address book's fields, with the gaps the lookup cannot fill. Behind it the lookup client calls the INS backend's /address-lookup endpoint, or, in stub mode, an in-memory stub returning three fixed addresses. Claims cover the page's registration and route, every element of the page in render order, the search-mode rules, the mapping rules and gaps, the client and stub, and every English and Welsh copy key (40 keys each).

claims.statement: The notifications dashboard is served at the root path / of the Import Notification Service frontend, on GET.
The dashboard's page title is 'Dashboard'.
The dashboard's main heading is 'Dashboard', shown as an extra-large heading.
The dashboard heading has no caption above it: the template renders only the h1.
The dashboard uses the wide 'display' content column rather than the standard form column.
claims.note: What 'display' resolves to is in shared/kit.js (part 4).

claims.statement: The dashboard has a search form that submits with GET back to the dashboard path /.
The search field is labelled 'Search by notification reference'.
The search field is a search-type text input named referenceNumber, two-thirds width, and is refilled with the reference the user last searched for.
claims.quote:
id: "referenceNumber",
      name: "referenceNumber",
      type: "search",
      value: referenceNumber,
      classes: "govuk-!-width-two-thirds"

claims.statement: The search field has no hint text.
claims.note: No hint key is passed to govukInput and none exists in copy.en.js.

claims.statement: The search button reads 'Search'.
Searching keeps the current sort order, because the search form carries the current sort as a hidden field.
A search returns the user to the first page of results, because neither the search form nor the sort form sends a page number.
The searched reference has surrounding spaces trimmed, and a blank search is treated as no search.
claims.quote:
const referenceNumber = request.query.referenceNumber?.trim() ?? ''
  const hasSearch = Boolean(referenceNumber)

claims.statement: The search has no validation and no error message: any text is passed to ins-backend as the reference to match.
claims.note: No validator, error summary or error message exists in the controller, template or copy.

claims.statement: The frontend does not say whether a reference search matches a whole reference or part of one; the match rule belongs to ins-backend. Only the stub defines it, as an exact whole-reference match.
The only way to narrow the list is the reference search: there is no filter by status, date, country or commodity.
A sort form is shown only when the current page has at least one notification row.
The sort select is labelled 'Sort by'.
The sort select offers four options, in order: 'Arrival date (newest first)', 'Arrival date (oldest first)', 'Last updated (newest first)', 'Last updated (oldest first)'.
claims.quote:
arrivalNewest: 'Arrival date (newest first)',
      arrivalOldest: 'Arrival date (oldest first)',
      updatedNewest: 'Last updated (newest first)',
      updatedOldest: 'Last updated (oldest first)'

claims.statement: The four sort options send the values arrivalDate,desc, arrivalDate,asc, lastUpdated,desc and lastUpdated,asc.
claims.quote:
{ value: 'arrivalDate,desc', copyKey: 'arrivalNewest' },
  { value: 'arrivalDate,asc', copyKey: 'arrivalOldest' },
  { value: 'lastUpdated,desc', copyKey: 'updatedNewest' },
  { value: 'lastUpdated,asc', copyKey: 'updatedOldest' }

claims.statement: The default sort is arrival date, newest first.
A sort value in the address that is not one of the four options is ignored and the default sort is used.
The sort select shows the sort currently in use as selected.
The sort form's button reads 'Update sort' and is a secondary button; the sort applies only when the user presses it.
Changing the sort keeps the current reference search, because the sort form carries the search as a hidden field.
The page number is read from the page query parameter; a missing, non-numeric or less-than-1 value shows page 1.
claims.quote:
const page = Number.parseInt(queryPage, 10)
  return Number.isNaN(page) || page < 1 ? 1 : page

claims.statement: When there are no notifications at all and no search is active, the dashboard shows the empty-state text 'There are no notifications yet.'
The empty state shows a 'Start a new notification' button link.
'Start a new notification' goes to the live-animals journey on the animals frontend: the configured animals frontend base URL followed by /live-animals.
The 'Start a new notification' button appears only in the empty state; a user who already has notifications has no start-a-new-notification link on the dashboard.
claims.note: The header or layout (part 4) may carry another way in; this template has none outside the empty state.

claims.statement: When a search finds nothing, the dashboard shows 'No notifications found'.
Below 'No notifications found' a 'Clear search' link returns the user to the unsearched dashboard at /.
When there are results, a results label above the table reads 'Showing {from}-{to} of {total}'.
The results label counts from (page - 1) x page size + 1 to the smaller of page x page size and the total, with the page clamped into the range of pages that exist.
claims.quote:
from: (currentPage - 1) * size + 1,
    to: Math.min(currentPage * size, totalElements),

claims.statement: When a search has results, a 'Clear search' link is shown above the table and returns the user to /.
The notifications table has the caption 'Notifications', hidden visually and read only by assistive technology.
The table's columns, in order, are 'Reference number', 'Status', 'Origin country', 'Commodity', 'Arrival date' and an action column.
claims.quote:
reference: 'Reference number',
    status: 'Status',
    origin: 'Origin country',
    commodity: 'Commodity',
    arrival: 'Arrival date',
    action: 'Action',

claims.statement: The action column's heading 'Action' is visually hidden.
The reference number column shows the notification's reference, such as GBN-AG-26-000001, as plain text.
The status column shows the raw status code from ins-backend, such as SUBMITTED, DRAFT or AMEND, as plain text: there is no status tag and no friendly status label.
claims.note: No govukTag import and no status copy keys exist; the fit spec asserts cells named 'SUBMITTED', 'DRAFT' and 'AMEND'.

claims.statement: The statuses the dashboard is seen to handle are SUBMITTED, DRAFT and AMEND, with DELETED hidden from the list; no complete list of statuses is defined in the frontend.
claims.note: Only the stub names the statuses, and only SUBMITTED gets special treatment in link building.

claims.statement: The origin country column shows the country's name from the countries service, falling back to the country code ins-backend returned when no name is found, and blank when there is none.
The commodity column shows the commodity ins-backend returns, or is blank when it has none.
The arrival date column shows the date in the form '10 Sep 2026' (day, short month, year), and is blank when the date is missing or invalid.
The table has no column for the last updated date, although the list can be sorted by it.
The table does not show which kind of notification (live animals, plants or other) a row is: there is no journey-type column.
Each row's action column has a 'View' link whose accessible name adds the reference number in visually hidden text, such as 'View GBN-AG-26-000001'.
A submitted notification's View link opens the read-only notification view on the animals frontend: {animals base URL}/live-animals/notifications/{reference}/notification-view.
Any notification not SUBMITTED (draft, amend or another status) has a View link back into its journey hub on the animals frontend: {animals base URL}/live-animals/notifications/{reference}.
The reference number is URL-encoded in the View link.
Every dashboard row links into the live-animals journey: there is no link into the plants journey, and the only journey set base defined is /live-animals.
claims.note: A plants notification shown on the dashboard would be linked into the live-animals journey; nothing in the slice routes by journey type.

claims.statement: The INS frontend has no notification view page of its own: opening a notification always leaves for the animals frontend.
Pagination is shown only when there is more than one page of results.
Pagination shows a numbered link for every page, marks the current page, and shows Previous and Next links except on the first and last page.
claims.note: Every page number is listed, with no ellipsis, however many pages there are.

claims.statement: Pagination links keep the current search and sort.
Dashboard links leave the default sort and page 1 out of the address, so the first page with the default sort is plain /.
The page size is not chosen by the frontend: it sends no size to ins-backend and uses the size ins-backend returns.
If loading the notifications or the country list fails, the dashboard still renders with its heading and search but no table, flags a recoverable error, and responds with HTTP status 500.
claims.note: How the recoverable error is shown to the user is in the shared layout (part 4).

claims.statement: A failure to load the dashboard is logged as an error with the message 'Failed to load dashboard'.
An HTTP error already shaped for the framework (a Boom error) is passed on rather than shown as the dashboard's recoverable error.
Every dashboard load reads the country list from the countries service, to turn origin country codes into names.
The dashboard reads notifications from ins-backend with GET {ins-backend base URL}/notifications.
The ins-backend request always sends the page number, and sends sort and referenceNumber query parameters only when set.
The ins-backend request carries the request's trace id in the configured tracing header.
A non-success response from ins-backend is treated as an error.
The dashboard expects ins-backend to return a page of notifications with content, page, size, totalElements and totalPages.
claims.quote:
page: response.page,
  size: response.size,
  totalElements: response.totalElements,
  totalPages: response.totalPages

claims.statement: Each notification the dashboard reads from ins-backend supplies referenceNumber, status, originCountry, commodity and arrivalDate.

The dashboard's request for notifications carries no organisation or user identity, so nothing in this frontend shows the list being limited to the signed-in user's organisation; any such scoping would have to happen elsewhere.
claims.note: Security finding, stated in general terms only. Who may see which notifications is not stated anywhere in the slice.

claims.statement: The dashboard reads from a built-in stub instead of ins-backend when stub mode is on, and never in production.

The stub holds four notifications: GBN-AG-26-000001 SUBMITTED (FR, Cattle, arriving 10 Sep 2026), GBN-AG-26-000002 DRAFT (IE, no commodity, 12 Sep 2026), GBN-AG-26-000003 AMEND (DE, no commodity, 8 Sep 2026) and GBN-AG-26-000004 DELETED (GB, no commodity, 9 Sep 2026).
Each stub notification also carries an aggregate id, an aggregate version and a last updated time, which the dashboard does not show.
The stub never returns a DELETED notification, so a deleted notification does not appear on the dashboard.
The stub's reference search matches the whole reference exactly and returns matches unsorted.
The stub sorts by arrival date or last updated, ascending or descending, defaulting to arrival date newest first.
The stub pages results 25 at a time and always reports at least one page.
The dashboard navigation section counts as current only on the exact path /.
claims.note: Used by the shared header (part 4) to mark the current navigation item.

claims.statement: Asking for a page number past the last page of results shows no table, no empty-state message and no sort form: the empty state appears only when there are no notifications at all, and the table and sort form only when the page has rows.

claims.statement: The address book list page is served by GET at /address-book.
The list, view and delete pages all require the signed-in session to carry an organisation id; without one the request fails with 403 Forbidden 'Organisation could not be identified'.

The search input's hint 'Search by name, town or city, postcode or country' is passed inside the label object rather than as the input's hint, so the GOV.UK input macro most likely does not render it.

claims.statement: One journey is registered for the handshake: journey type 'gbn-ag'.
The 'gbn-ag' journey returns to the animals frontend, at its configured base URL plus the '/live-animals' journey set base.
The return path into the journey is /notifications/{notification-id}/address-return?fulfilment-id={fulfilment-id}, with both ids URL-encoded.
A journey sends the user to the add page with four query parameters: journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token.
claims.quote:
journeyType: queryValue(request, 'journey-type'),
    notificationId: queryValue(request, 'notification-id'),

claims.statement: Handshake parameter values are trimmed, and a blank value counts as absent.
The handshake parameters must be sent all together or not at all: some but not all of them gives a 400 'Incomplete journey handshake' error.
A handshake with a journey type that is not registered shows the page not found error.

The return URL is never taken from the request: it is built on the server from the registered journey's configured base URL and path template, so a journey cannot send the user back to an arbitrary address.
claims.note: Inferred: the only check on the return destination is that the journey type is in the registry; the ids are encoded into a fixed template.

claims.statement: The address book does not verify the handshake token, notification id or fulfilment id; it only carries them and passes them back to the journey.
claims.note: Inferred: no code in the slice checks the token's value; verifying it is presumably the journey frontend's job on return.

claims.statement: Opening the add page with a valid handshake stores the journey context in the user's session; opening it with no handshake parameters clears any stored journey context.

On submit, journey context in the form takes precedence and is re-stored in the session; if the form carries none, the context stored in the session is used, and a stored context with an unregistered journey type is discarded.

one line in [`routes.js`](../routes.js) — no permanent feature depends
on it.

claims.statement: The page decides the search mode itself from what was typed: a term that looks like a full UK postcode is searched as a postcode, and anything else is searched as free text. The user is never asked to pick a mode.
A postcode is matched case-insensitively, with or without a space between its halves.
A postcode term is normalised before searching: spaces removed, upper-cased, and one space put before the last three characters (so 'sw1a1aa' searches as 'SW1A 1AA').
claims.quote:
Upper case with a single space before the final three characters, which is how the
 * lookup returns postcodes and how it expects to be asked. Lets "sw1a1aa" find
 * something rather than silently returning nothing.

claims.statement: To build the address lines, the result's premises are its sub-building name then building name, joined by ', ', and its street is its building number then street, joined by a space.

Premises first, then the street. Sub-building before building name because that is
 * the order they read in ("Unit 1, Downing House"), and a number binds to its street
 * ("1 Downing Street") rather than standing alone.

claims.statement: When a result has both premises and a street, address line 1 is the premises and address line 2 is the street followed by the locality, joined by ', '.
When a result has only premises or only a street, that becomes address line 1 and the locality becomes address line 2.
When a result has no name, number or street, address line 1 falls back to the whole formatted address line, and address line 2 is the locality.
The result's town fills 'Town or city' and its postcode fills 'Postcode'.
County and country are always left empty by the mapping, because the lookup returns no county and only a free-text country name.

claims.statement: The lookup client calls the INS backend's GET /address-lookup endpoint, passing the search as a query parameter: postcode=<postcode> for a postcode search or find=<term> for a free-text search.
The lookup client can also call /address-lookup with no query parameters, for the backend's default postcode; the spike page does not use this call.
Each lookup request carries the request's trace ID in the configured tracing header, so the backend's work can be followed in the logs.
A lookup response with an error status is treated as a failed request.

A lookup response carries an outcome (RESULTS, NO_RESULTS or FAILED), the results, the total and returned result counts, a failure reason, and optionally the backend's timings (STS, Entra, lookup and total milliseconds, and whether the token was cached).
claims.quote:
outcome: 'RESULTS',
  query: { mode, term },
  results: RESULTS,
  totalResults: RESULTS.length,
  returnedResults: RESULTS.length,
  failureReason: null
claims.note: Shape read from the stub's response and the fields the controller and template read; the timings shape comes from the controller destructuring { stsMs, entraMs, lookupMs, totalMs, tokenSource }.
